task: Harden release parent merge-to-main CI execution with exact merged-head dispatch, durable auditable run evidence and fail-closed restart closure.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Issue #1156: canonical parent release executor uses its GITHUB_TOKEN to squash-merge parent PR and marks MERGED/PARENT_CLOSED instantly. GitHub suppresses automatic push CI for that token, leaving a missing exact merged main CI while falsely completing the execution chain. The fix must independently bind an explicitly dispatched exact-head main workflow run to the persisted parent source/merge identity and await successful terminal evidence.
observableOutcomes: After a trusted parent merge, the canonical release state remains pending until a separately dispatched CI run on the actual merged main SHA completes SUCCESS.
The exact workflow run ID, immutable source commit, merged main SHA, branch, event, workflow identity, status and terminal conclusion are recorded in durable canonical state.
A restarted executor safely resumes a persisted pending dispatch without starting duplicate workflows or accepting earlier unrelated successful runs.
Wrong branch, wrong source SHA, changed main, wrong run ID, stale run, forged actor/nonce, missing CI, declined dispatch, failed or cancelled CI block or remain pending with explicit error.
Legacy canonical MERGED parent receipts are not rewritten and the source 65e52ffd, U01-U03 close receipts and their protected evidence remain immutable.
Exact-head PR/main CI and negative regression tests verify the fix before deployment.
unresolvedRisks: GitHub Actions-token merge has no push trigger: workflow_dispatch must be explicit and authenticated by trusted executor authority.
A dispatch may take time to appear in run listing, and an executor can be interrupted between dispatch and receipt persistence.
Any main ref advance before dispatch can cause a workflow to target the wrong code; require exact merged-head matching, otherwise block.
Manually triggered CI on the same SHA can be unrelated; discriminate via deterministic parent transaction and merge nonce and the run's event/branch/identity.
The canonical state must be persisted between merge, dispatch and terminal CI result via existing CAS; do not infer success from a dispatched signal.

Late review of PR #1166 revealed a cross-system crash window: GH workflow_dispatch may succeed while the canonical CAS write of DISPATCH_REQUESTED has not yet happened. On restart, the persisted INTENT_RECORDED state plus a delayed GitHub listing could trigger a second dispatch. The GitHub API does not offer a transactionally idempotent workflow_dispatch call.

in: Add a durable parent post-merge CI pending lifecycle and exact receipt to canonical release executor.
Explicitly dispatch CI on main, with an exact parent/merge correlation marker and no child-proof flag.
Bind exact run ID, event, head SHA, branch, title and conclusion; require terminal success before PARENT_CLOSED.
Add trusted CI workflow_dispatch marker and verify its input/main SHA identity.
Cover interrupted PR merge recovery and dispatch retry without accepting forged/stale runs.
Adversarial regression scenarios and integration wiring tests.
out: No change to immutable rehearsal source, source branch, child state or receipt evidence.
No manual edit to canonical remote state or GitHub workflows outside the CI binding.
No unrelated storefront, builder, templates or production runtime features.
No broad bypass for CI, Truth, Lifecycle or failure-intake requirements.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The gap is a state/authority race between GitHub Actions-token merges and separately dispatched CI, requiring explicit asynchronous transaction identities, durable recovery, input authentication and exact-head success evidence.

acceptanceCriteria: Pre-code plan passes the canonical Plan Before Code Gate and any measured scope corrections are made in plan-only commits.
A canonical merged parent PR produces POST_MERGE_CI_PENDING, not MERGED, with exact merge SHA and source-bound dispatch nonce.
The next persisted executor step dispatches CI via workflow_dispatch on main and records/reuses one exact run ID per parent merge.
Wrong SHA/branch/event/workflow/name/nonce/actor, missing or failed run and stale unrelated success cannot transition to MERGED.
Terminal SUCCESS on the exact merged main SHA yields persisted CI evidence and only then PARENT_CLOSED.
Resumption after post-merge-but-pre-persistence interruption is fail-closed and validates original PR/proof before accepting merge.
Full quality tests, TypeScript, build, Truth/Lifecycle and exact-head PR/main CI reach SUCCESS before merge.

Persist a one-shot dispatch authorization before invoking the GitHub workflow_dispatch side effect. A restart from any uncertain state MUST NOT issue another dispatch automatically; it can only reconcile the uniquely correlated run or fail closed awaiting operator review.
invariants: MERGED and PARENT_CLOSED for new closures require independently confirmed CI SUCCESS on exact mergedMainSha.
PENDING/dispatch attempted are not success, even if GitHub accepted the dispatch request.
Source commit, parent identity, U01-U03 child receipts and canonical proof remain unchanged and must match.
Duplicate dispatches are not created for a previously recorded correlation token or run ID.
No use of arbitrary prior successful main CI as canonical merge receipt.
Latest main HEAD must equal mergedMainSha at the moment workflow dispatch is authorized.
Only the canonical trusted executor persists remote state with CAS.
forbiddenStates: PARENT_CLOSED immediately after GITHUB_TOKEN merge without a main CI run.
Foreign manual or unrelated workflow run with matching SHA is treated as proof.
A failed/cancelled or in-progress run is recorded as PASS.
Two simultaneous or duplicate dispatches on retry with identical parent identity.
A forged branch/source, missing child receipt or changed main is accepted.
A CI run started against different main SHA is incorrectly attributed to the merge.
Two workflow_dispatch calls can originate from the same persisted INTENT_RECORDED state when GitHub run-list visibility is delayed or an executor crashes after the first dispatch.

failureModes: GITHUB_TOKEN squash merge suppresses push CI.
Merge completes but state CAS fails, leaving PR_OPEN with merged remote.
Dispatch is acknowledged but workflow run is initially invisible.
The executor crashes after dispatch before recording run ID.
A previous user-initiated main CI on the same SHA is mistakenly adopted.
A CI run targets a subsequent main SHA after merge races.
Runner actor/title/workflow inputs differ from the canonical dispatch intention.
Workflow fails or is cancelled while executor polls.
Atomicity gap between accepted external GitHub workflow_dispatch and canonical state CAS can produce duplicate accepted workflow events without an idempotency key.
edgeCases: No new CI trigger after GITHUB_TOKEN merge.
Existing post-merge CI in progress for same unique nonce.
Run not yet visible after a successful dispatch.
Sole unrelated manual SUCCESS on same main commit.
Malformed/foreign run ID, name, branch, actor, title or event.
Changed main branch between merge and dispatch.
Interrupted after PR merged but before canonical state persisted.
Interrupted after dispatch but before run ID persisted.
Exact correlated run finishes FAILED or CANCELLED.
Legacy already-MERGED persisted state from before #1156.
A second retry sees SUCCESS without duplicating workflow.
Exactly between GitHub accepting workflow_dispatch and the executor persisting a run ID / DISPATCH_REQUESTED state; a restart must not dispatch again even if GitHub run-list is temporarily empty.
Exactly between durable dispatch authorization CAS and the GH network request; the executor must prefer explicit uncertainty over an unsafe automatic retry.

alternatives.summary: Persist pending state, dispatch correlated exact-commit main CI and prove terminal success before MERGED.
alternatives.reason: Establishes a durable, independently checked downstream proof boundary and supports guarded resumability.

alternatives.summary: Call workflow_dispatch immediately after merge and mark parent CLOSED without waiting.
alternatives.reason: Would retain the existing false success claim and could not detect failed/misrouted CI.

alternatives.summary: Create empty commit on main to force a push CI.
alternatives.reason: Changes main identity, consumes builds and breaks the exact merge SHA binding.

alternatives.summary: Accept any existing green main CI run with the same SHA.
alternatives.reason: Admits stale or manually initiated runs unrelated to the release parent closure.

specialistReviews.finding: GITHUB_TOKEN squash-merge suppression prevents the expected push-triggered verification. The network dispatch side effect is not idempotent if the execution crashes before persisting the run response.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use explicit workflow_dispatch tied to persisted merged main identity, and wait for exact run result. Persist a one-shot authorization CAS before dispatch, and never resend automatically when the result may already have been accepted.

specialistReviews.finding: A self-declared successful dispatch or a pre-existing green main run could be forged into a release claim.
specialistReviews.resolution: Correlate parent ID + source + merged SHA via nonce, require exact run identity and terminal success, block unbound runs.

specialistReviews.finding: A GitHub merge and canonical release-state commit are independent side effects that can be interrupted.
specialistReviews.resolution: Represent pending states explicitly and recover only with exact PR/merge proofs and compare-and-swap persistence.

specialistReviews.finding: No existing regression exercises the post-merge exact-head main CI path.
specialistReviews.resolution: Exercise valid, wrong SHA, stale, failed, noncanonical and crash/retry transitions without weakening baseline guards.

specialistReviews.finding: The new dependency must remain in DOMAIN-RELEASE instead of leaking release authority into quality runtime.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep dispatch and state transition in trusted executor; CI only validates its own dispatch identity.

challenge.finding: Risk: GH Actions-token merge is not sufficient evidence.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Explicitly dispatch CI and defer MERGED.

challenge.finding: Risk: Unrelated manual green CI can share SHA.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Require nonce, run ID and matching exact run metadata.

challenge.finding: Risk: Target main could advance after squash merge.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Compare remote main SHA to exact mergedMainSha pre-dispatch.

challenge.scenario: Scenario: GitHub accepts the workflow_dispatch request for SHA S and run-name N but gh run list returns zero matching runs on the next poll; the executor crashes and resumes.
challenge.finding: Risk: An immediate second dispatch would create duplicate CI runs and could adopt an unrelated run with the same commit SHA.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Persist DISPATCH_REQUESTED with deterministic N before re-query; retain PENDING on zero results and accept only N-bound run with exact event, SHA and branch.

challenge.finding: Risk: No persisted run id but event exists.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Recover by nonce and stable run identity without duplicate.

challenge.finding: Risk: GitHub PR merged before canonical state CAS.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Recover only exact merged PR/source/proof binding.

challenge.finding: Risk: A failed job must not close parent.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Block with terminal failure details.

challenge.scenario: Scenario: An ordinary user triggers a successful CI workflow_dispatch on main SHA S, copies the canonical parent run-name token N, but the workflow actor is not github-actions[bot].
challenge.finding: Risk: Selecting the run by SHA and title alone would forge a bot-executor release receipt.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Validate actor, workflow file/name, run ID, event, exact main SHA and persisted nonce together; reject any user-actor or foreign run.

challenge.finding: Risk: Prior green main run is unrelated.
Risk: Pre-hardening receipts already marked MERGED.
challenge.resolution: Resolution: Do not mutate old receipts; gate only new pending transitions.

challenge.scenario: A workflow_dispatch completes server-side, but the runner crashes before it persists DISPATCH_REQUESTED; an immediate retry sees zero runs because the GitHub list API has eventual consistency.
challenge.finding: Existing implementation checks only INTENT_RECORDED then dispatches again, violating at-most-once behavior despite otherwise valid exact-head proof.
challenge.resolution: Introduce a durable pre-dispatch one-shot reservation; execute the side effect only in the same CAS-winning process after persistence. On uncertain resume, list/poll the nonce-bound run, never auto-dispatch again. Document rare fail-closed manual recovery if a crash happens after reservation but before GitHub accepts the call.

proofPlan: Validate complete plan and fail-closed dependency scope on a plan-only commit.
Implement durable transition from successful PR merge to POST_MERGE_CI_PENDING (not CLOSED).
Add deterministic correlation workflow_dispatch input and runtime verification of target main identity.
Implement run-ID evidence, exact-status polling, retry idempotence and canonical state persistence.
Exercise positive end-to-end state evolution and negative spoof, stale, wrong SHA, failed run and crash/resume cases.
Run Quality, TypeScript, Production build, Plan, Edit-Time, Incremental Replay, Truth and Lifecycle checks at exact head.
Open PR only after branch proof; require exact-head PR CI then merge with approval gate.
Verify merged main exact-head CI and do not mutate original source/receipts.
Add explicit fault-injection regression for crash after accepted dispatch before run-ID CAS and a stale/empty run-list response; assert exactly one network dispatch and PENDING/BLOCK after restart.
Reopen previously closed plan for measured critical race, then require Plan Before Code PASS before implementing pre-dispatch durable reservation and exact-head lifecycle re-verification.

requirements.requirement: Parent release is DONE only when a trusted, persisted exact-merged-main CI execution has terminal success evidence.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Wrong SHA or stale unrelated SUCCESS cannot be accepted.
PARENT_CLOSED is forbidden until exact correlated run is SUCCESS.
Interruptions and retry neither duplicate workflow nor forge canonical state.

notes: Issue #1156: bot-merge post-merge main CI execution edge, source #65e52ffd... immutable, U01-U03 CLOSED. Last known main 5a39a1d8f31458d45617d3246b77ec3740db19d0 and CI #9261 SUCCESS; do not change their proof. Plan-only before implementation. Old #182 queued without jobs is independently isolated and not part of this release claim. No changes to canonical state outside entrusted executor runtime. Plan-only CI #9263 measured 19 expected failure IDs including 9 Template Factory inherited release regressions and digest 128614ad. Corrected canonical Release/Known Failure reviewer roles and two concrete adversarial challenge cases prior to code edit. CI #9265 measured one Sentinel integrity failure: CAP-RELEASE was asserted by Plan/Edit-Time guards that prove CAP-QUALITY, and 'execution/audit/resumability' dimensions were not in their proof semantics. Preserved CAP-RELEASE but rebound claim to actual GUARD-RELEASE-RISK plus wildcard GUARD-QUALITY-TESTS/PRODUCTION-BUILD, and to the supported exact proof dimensions. GitHub REST run.name also reflects run-name marker; the run verifier now binds this unique title and does not rely on GH CLI workflowName output. PR #1166 exact-head review identified a critical remaining at-most-once dispatch crash window even though #9267 branch-CI was SUCCESS. The previous LEARN/VERIFIED claim is reopened, not kept as DONE, until a pre-dispatch CAS reservation and negative fault-injection tests are implemented and fully reverified. Existing immutable rehearsal source and closed receipts must remain unchanged.
